capabilities: Track part-time shifts with pay split into morning, day, evening and late-night rates per store
Warn before saving a shift that pushes any 7-day window over the 28-hour student limit
Sync shift events to macOS Calendar or export .ics for Google Calendar, Outlook or a phone
Read shift rosters from selected text or photos via a user-configured AI service
Save a Markdown pay note with totals by store and overtime to check against a payslip
extras: Free and MIT-licensed, desktop only (Obsidian 1.13+); calendar sync requires macOS while .ics export works anywhere; optional AI roster reading is billed by the user's own provider and uses shell (osascript) calls to Apple Calendar, which the directory flags as Shell Execution; interface is Chinese or English only; the 28-hour rules are stated to be for reference only.
problem: Obsidian has no way to log part-time shifts, estimate Japanese-style pay (late-night, overtime, holiday premiums) and enforce the 28-hour weekly work limit for students.

relations.evidence: Sync to macOS Calendar from the ⋯ menu: smart sync writes only changed shifts

requires.name: AI provider key for roster reading (DeepSeek, Gemini, OpenAI, etc.)

summary: Shift tracker for part-time work in Japan that computes pay by time band and store, warns before any 7-day window exceeds the 28-hour student limit, and syncs to macOS Calendar.
